records.name: West Bengal
records.summary:
West Bengal replicates the checkpoint script documented in its neighbour: police arrested a transgender person arriving from across the long, porous international border for allegedly "infiltrating", treating trans presentation as evidence of illegal entry rather than identity. It is also one of only three states recording cases under the Transgender Persons Act in 2021 (3 of 7 nationally), indicating that some legal infrastructure exists but also that trans-targeted crime occurs at a detectable rate.

The border profiling is visitor-facing and state-actor-driven, but the incidents are fewer and less concentrated than a repeated-sweep pattern elsewhere: the documented record here is a single arrest plus the broader infiltration framing. For a foreign visitor transiting the land border, the primary exposure is the same appearance-as-suspicion-trigger mechanism - trans presentation treated as evidence of illegal entry.

sources.summary: NOTE: page not retrievable at fetch time (access-denied block); the underlying East Bengal report covers South Dinajpur police arresting "Ali Mondal aka Bijli Mondal," a Bangladeshi transgender person from Sirajganj district, for allegedly infiltrating India, along with the e-rickshaw driver who brought her across the border.

Queerbeat crime-data report (30 Jan 2026), West Bengal row: of the 7 Transgender Persons Act cases nationally in 2021, 3 were registered in West Bengal (highest that year alongside Assam/Kerala) — detectable-rate crime plus the report's caveat that national counts are tiny (20 cases 2019-23) from police-registration bias, and 2025 survey prevalence of 27.2% physical / 22.3% sexual violence.

The Quint (5 November 2024) publishes an RTI investigation into transgender welfare boards: West Bengal is one of the 12 states/UTs that notified a board, but the majority of boards have held fewer than one meeting per year since their creation, and the 17 existing boards 'are mostly running rudderless without a policy framework, compliance mechanism, or any power', with several functioning as non-transparent bodies that diffuse demands instead of serving trans people. Supports this record's claim that West Bengal's constituted welfare board operates without a functioning policy framework.

Times of India, Kolkata (18 August 2024): a group of trans women heading to RG Kar Medical College filed an FIR alleging an RPF constable at Rabindra Sadan metro station groped one of them 'to check her gender' and made inappropriate remarks. Metro Railway and the RPF denied the allegations and counter-filed an FIR against the group, while footage showed the trans woman in tears. Documents the state-actor gender-checking conduct this record associates with West Bengal's policing of trans people.

records.name: Tamil Nādu
records.summary: Tamil Nadu is the country's most protective sub-national regime for trans visitors. It was the first state to introduce a transgender welfare policy (1995), maintains a dedicated Transgender Welfare Board, and adopted a comprehensive State Policy for Transgender Persons in 2025. On 4 August 2025 the Madras High Court expressly commended the policy as "a victory for transgender and intersex persons after their long struggle" - active judicial confirmation of executive protection that is rare and meaningful for a visitor's institutional recourse. The state was also the only one recording a Transgender Persons Act case in 2020 (1 of 1 nationally) and logged 7 of the 11 national cases in 2023 - its courts are demonstrably being used.

sources.summary: Official Tamil Nadu transgender-welfare portal: publishes the gender-change application kit (affidavit form, certificate of identity for change of gender, membership ID relaxation, user manuals) and documents the state regime — first Indian state with a transgender welfare policy, free sex-reassignment surgery in government hospitals, housing and citizenship-scheme access, and the thirunangai/thirunambi administrative categories embedded in governance.

NOTE: page not retrievable at fetch time (never cached); the underlying document is the Madras High Court order of 4 August 2025 (WP 7284 of 2021) noting with approval that the state brought into effect the Tamil Nadu State Policy for Transgender Persons 2025, calling it "a victory for transgender and intersex persons after their long struggle" and expressly commending the government.

Queerbeat crime-data report (30 Jan 2026), Tamil Nadu rows: the only state with a Transgender Persons Act case in 2020 (1 of 1 nationally) and in 2022 (1), and 7 of the 11 national cases in 2023 — courts demonstrably reachable in this state, against the report's registration-bias caveat.
